lines.text: Asaph asks why God's anger smolders against the sheep of His pasture, and he asks God to remember Mount Sinai.
God's foes roared in His meeting place, smashed all the carvings with hatchets and picks, and burned the sanctuary to the ground.
The enemy burned every meeting place, no priest remains, and Asaph asks how long the enemy will taunt God.
God is Asaph's King from ancient times, who divided the sea and crushed the heads of Leviathan.
Asaph asks God not to forget His afflicted, to consider His covenant, and to let the poor and needy praise His name.
